# Titus {.unnumbered}

##### Chapter 1

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Titus" data-chapter="1">
<p><span class="drop-cap">P</span>aul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness; <span class="verse-number">2</span> In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began; <span class="verse-number">3</span> But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour; <span class="verse-number">4</span> To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour. <span class="verse-number">5</span> For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee: <span class="verse-number">6</span> If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly. <span class="verse-number">7</span> For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; <span class="verse-number">8</span> But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate; <span class="verse-number">9</span> Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers. <span class="verse-number">10</span> For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: <span class="verse-number">11</span> Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake. <span class="verse-number">12</span> One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies. <span class="verse-number">13</span> This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith; <span class="verse-number">14</span> Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. <span class="verse-number">16</span> They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Titus][1]
\lettrine[lines=4]{P}{aul,} a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;
\vs{2}In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;
\vs{3}But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour;
\vs{4}To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
\vs{5}For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:
\vs{6}If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.
\vs{7}For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;
\vs{8}But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;
\vs{9}Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.
\vs{10}For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision:
\vs{11}Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.
\vs{12}One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.
\vs{13}This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;
\vs{14}Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.
\vs{15}Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.
\vs{16}They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 2

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Titus" data-chapter="2">
<p><span class="drop-cap">B</span>ut speak thou the things which become sound doctrine: <span class="verse-number">2</span> That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience. <span class="verse-number">3</span> The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things; <span class="verse-number">4</span> That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, <span class="verse-number">5</span> To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded. <span class="verse-number">7</span> In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, <span class="verse-number">8</span> Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again; <span class="verse-number">10</span> Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things. <span class="verse-number">11</span> For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, <span class="verse-number">12</span> Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; <span class="verse-number">13</span> Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; <span class="verse-number">14</span> Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works. <span class="verse-number">15</span> These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Titus][2]
\lettrine[lines=4]{B}{ut} speak thou the things which become sound doctrine:
\vs{2}That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.
\vs{3}The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;
\vs{4}That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,
\vs{5}To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.
\vs{6}Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded.
\vs{7}In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,
\vs{8}Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.
\vs{9}Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again;
\vs{10}Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.
\vs{11}For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,
\vs{12}Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;
\vs{13}Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
\vs{14}Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
\vs{15}These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 3

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Titus" data-chapter="3">
<p><span class="drop-cap">P</span>ut them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, <span class="verse-number">2</span> To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. <span class="verse-number">3</span> For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. <span class="verse-number">4</span> But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, <span class="verse-number">5</span> Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; <span class="verse-number">6</span> Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; <span class="verse-number">7</span> That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. <span class="verse-number">8</span> This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men. <span class="verse-number">9</span> But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain. <span class="verse-number">10</span> A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; <span class="verse-number">11</span> Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself. <span class="verse-number">12</span> When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them. <span class="verse-number">14</span> And let our's also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful. <span class="verse-number">15</span> All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Titus][3]
\lettrine[lines=4]{P}{ut} them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work,
\vs{2}To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
\vs{3}For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
\vs{4}But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,
\vs{5}Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;
\vs{6}Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;
\vs{7}That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
\vs{8}This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.
\vs{9}But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.
\vs{10}A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;
\vs{11}Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.
\vs{12}When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.
\vs{13}Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.
\vs{14}And let our's also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.
\vs{15}All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
\end{scripture}
:::
